titleZh: 凯文·波拉克的访谈节目
summaryEn: A long-form 2009 conversation recorded days after the Tesla Model S sedan was unveiled. Musk talks through the case for electric cars, his passion for rockets, and the early struggles of Tesla and SpaceX.
summaryZh: 这是一场录制于2009年的长篇对谈，时间是在 Tesla Model S 轿车发布后的几天。马斯克详述了支持电动汽车的理由、他对火箭的热爱，以及 Tesla 和 SpaceX 早期的艰难历程。

segments.textEn: My next guest, I'm going to give you a little bit of a heads up in terms of who this next gentleman is and also admit that I am coming to this interview, I think, with the freshest eyes that he's probably faced in a while. That is to say, I was an instant fan when I found out about what this man has done, but I wanted to have him on so that I could ask the. The real straightforward, simple questions, which is one of the reasons I wanted to do this show, which is to not only meet people that I admired as well as have people on that I've worked with, but when I meet people and they know me from movies or what have you, they all want to know, really the hardships and how you got from there to here, and then they want to hear about your project.
segments.textZh: 我的下一位嘉宾，我先给大家简单介绍一下接下来这位先生是谁，同时也承认，我来做这次采访时，我想，我可能是他一段时间以来面对过的、对他了解最少的人。也就是说，当我了解到这个人的所作所为时，我立刻成了他的粉丝，但我想请他来，这样我就可以问那个。那些真正直截了当、简单的问题，这也是我想做这个节目的原因之一，也就是不仅要见到我钦佩的人，也要邀请与我合作过的人，但当我遇到人们，而他们从电影或诸如此类的东西中认识我时，他们其实都想知道那些艰辛，以及你是如何从那里走到这里的，然后他们还想听听你的项目。

segments.textEn: So I think that's where we're going to start today. And I'm going to now welcome the founder and CEO of Tesla Motors as well as SpaceX. I hope I pronounced those correctly.
segments.textZh: 所以我想，我们今天就从这里开始。现在，让我们欢迎 Tesla Motors 以及 SpaceX 的创始人兼首席执行官。我希望我的发音都正确。

segments.textEn: Yes, absolutely.
segments.textZh: 对，完全正确。

segments.textEn: And Elon Musk is also. Yeah, okay, good.
segments.textZh: 还有埃隆·马斯克也是。对，好，很好。

segments.textEn: So thank you very much. First of all, you're welcome for, for joining us here. And I also have to thank you profusely for not bolting out the door after watching the last four minutes of my show.
segments.textZh: 所以非常感谢你。首先，欢迎你，欢迎你来这里参加我们的节目。我还必须万分感谢你，看完我节目刚才那4分钟之后没有夺门而出。

segments.textEn: It was difficult.
segments.textZh: 这很难。

segments.textEn: It must have been.
segments.textZh: 肯定很难。

segments.textEn: Yeah, yeah.
segments.textZh: 对，对。

segments.textEn: Because it's very different world. And I'm sure that there was a moment, at least a moment, one in your mind, that said, oh, my God,
segments.textZh: 因为这是个截然不同的世界。而且我敢肯定，曾经有那么一刻，至少有那么一刻，你脑子里有个念头说，哦，我的天，

segments.textEn: what am I doing here?
segments.textZh: 我在这里干什么？

segments.textEn: What have I gotten myself into? Well, here's the thing. These, these interviews. Have you been on Charlie Rose yet?
segments.textZh: 我到底让自己卷进什么事里了？好吧，事情是这样的。这些，这些采访。你上过查理·罗斯的节目了吗？

segments.textEn: No, but I will be, I think later this month or early next.
segments.textZh: 没有，但我会上的，我想是在这个月晚些时候或下个月初。

segments.textEn: Yeah, yeah.
segments.textZh: 对，对。

segments.textEn: Well, watch the show.
segments.textZh: 好吧，看看这个节目。

segments.textEn: Yeah, yeah. As a viewer, you understand that one of the wonderful things about his show that I'm trying so desperately to emulate blatantly is actual conversations. Throughout my career, I've been fortunate enough to do almost every talk show that's existed for the last 20 years, starting with Johnny Carson and Larry King and all of them. And they're all about little sound bites and they're all about little quick anecdotes, in my case, with punchlines and characters.
segments.textZh: 对，对。作为一名观众，你明白他的节目有一个很棒的地方，而我正在极其拼命且明目张胆地模仿，那就是真实的对话。在我的职业生涯中，我很幸运，过去20年里几乎所有存在过的访谈节目我都上过，从约翰尼·卡森和拉里·金开始，还有所有那些节目。而它们关注的都是简短的声音片段，关注的都是简短的小轶事，就我而言，还要有笑点和人物模仿。

segments.textEn: Rarely is there an opportunity to have an actual conversation and to find out more details about what it is that drives you to do what you do and got you to the place that you're at today. So thank you very much for everything you're about to share. We've got twitter.com asking questions live. We've got folks actually very excited to ask questions. I'm going to start pretty much with, you know, reading a lot about you in preparation.
segments.textZh: 很少有机会进行一次真正的交谈，并进一步了解到底是什么驱使你去做你所做的事，又是什么让你走到今天这个位置。所以非常感谢你即将分享的一切。twitter.com 上有人正在实时提问。确实有很多人非常兴奋地想提问题。我要从，基本上就是，你知道，为了准备这次采访而读了很多关于你的资料开始。

segments.textEn: All that stuff is, you know, Wikipedia and various sites to find out one's history. How old were you?
segments.textZh: 那些东西都是，你知道，维基百科和各种网站，用来了解一个人的经历。你当时多大？

segments.textEn: It's all hit or miss.
segments.textZh: 那些东西全都时准时不准。

segments.textEn: I know it's all hit or miss. I find it to be that way. How old were you, if I may? Let's just start here. When the first vision popped into your head about working and bringing an electric car to the consumer.
segments.textZh: 我知道全都时准时不准。我发现确实如此。如果可以问的话，你当时多大？我们就从这里开始。你第一次产生致力于将电动汽车带给消费者的构想时。

segments.textEn: Well, I've been interested in electric cars for a long time. Actually, I used to think about it quite a bit in college. So it's been probably 17, 18 years that I've been thinking about the area. In fact, I used to talk to my dates in college about the importance of electric cars.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我对电动汽车感兴趣已经很久了。实际上，我上大学时就经常思考这件事。所以，我思考这个领域大概已经有17、18年了。事实上，我上大学约会时还会跟约会对象谈论电动汽车的重要性。

segments.textEn: And how did that work out for you? Not well.
segments.textZh: 那对你来说效果怎么样？不太好。

segments.textEn: It's not a great date conversation. No, no.
segments.textZh: 这不是什么很适合约会的话题。不，不。

segments.textEn: In fact, I ran into someone who I briefly dated in college and she brought this up, and she's a writer for Scientific American these days and come to do an interview with me and actually mentioned that it was a memorable date.
segments.textZh: 事实上，我遇到了一位大学时短暂约会过的人，她提起了这件事，她如今是《科学美国人》的撰稿人，来采访我，而且还真的提到那是一次令人难忘的约会。

segments.textEn: Not necessarily in a good way. Right.
segments.textZh: 不一定是从好的方面来说。对。

segments.textEn: One she would never forget.
segments.textZh: 一次她永远不会忘记的约会。

segments.textEn: Yeah, absolutely. But I'm kind of a science and engineering guy. So for me, it's been obvious for a while that the future we have to figure out a way to get off oil and that the solution is electric cars. The advantage of an electric car is that you can generate that electricity by renewable means. And so if you consume the electricity, if you're running electric cars and then you're generating your power with solar, wind, geothermal, which is increasing dramatically, by the way.
segments.textZh: 对，完全没错。但我算是个科学和工程领域的人。所以对我来说，有一件事早就很明显了：未来我们必须想办法摆脱石油，而解决方案就是电动汽车。电动汽车的优势在于，你可以通过可再生方式发电。因此，如果你使用电力，如果你在驾驶电动汽车，然后又用太阳能、风能、地热能来发电，顺便说一句，地热能正在大幅增长。

segments.textEn: It sure is.
segments.textZh: 确实如此。

segments.textEn: And if you're doing that, then you have a sustainable solution for the future. And obviously, if you're burning oil, that's something that's going to end sooner or later. And so it's better to do it sooner and avoid the environmental damage than later and have the environmental damage plus a massive wealth transfer from the United States to other countries.
segments.textZh: 如果你这样做，那么你就有了一个面向未来的可持续解决方案。很显然，如果你在燃烧石油，那它迟早会耗尽。因此，与其晚些时候再做，既造成环境破坏，又发生财富从美国向其他国家的大规模转移，不如早点做，避免环境破坏。

segments.textEn: Yeah, well, that's a big part of it too, is how do we take back control of our destiny, quite frankly. And so this idea came to you 17, 18 years ago. I think it was around that time that for the most part, those who were starting to hear rumblings of an electric car, myself included, were thinking whoever puts out a gorgeous as well as functional electric car wins in terms of exciting first a few and then the masses eventually with as the prices become more affordable to all consumers.
segments.textZh: 对，好吧，那也是其中很重要的一部分，坦白说，就是我们如何重新掌控自己的命运。所以这个想法是在17、18年前出现在你脑海里的。我想大约就在那个时候，包括我在内，那些开始听到电动汽车风声的人大多都在想，无论是谁，只要推出一辆既漂亮又实用的电动汽车，谁就会胜出，也就是说，先让少数人兴奋起来，然后随着价格变得所有消费者都更能负担得起，最终让大众也兴奋起来。

segments.textEn: Initially, what people are praising and also damning, you know, there's both sides of it. Initially you started with the Roadster, Right, The Tesla Roadster, which a huge success.
segments.textZh: 起初，人们既有称赞，也有谴责，你知道，两边都有。起初你们从 Roadster 开始，对吧，Tesla Roadster，一个巨大的成功。

segments.textEn: It has been very successful. Yeah.
segments.textZh: 它非常成功。对。

segments.textEn: How. Just walk us through, if you wouldn't mind, the chronological pieces of business here, because this really is fascinating to a great many of us. From conception to rolling out that first model. Just in terms of a brief history of the. I can't imagine the hardships that took place in trying to get this thing to come to fruition.
segments.textZh: 怎么做到的。请按时间顺序带我们了解一下这些商业环节，如果你不介意的话，因为这对我们很多人来说确实非常引人入胜。从构想到推出第一款车型。简单讲讲……的历史。我无法想象在试图让这件事成为现实时经历了多少艰难困苦。

segments.textEn: Yeah, it's certainly been technically quite difficult from a business standpoint. Quite difficult. And then it's been overlaid with a bit of a sort of soap opera from a personnel standpoint.
segments.textZh: 是的，从技术角度看，这当然相当困难。从商业角度看，也相当困难。然后在人事方面，又叠加了一点类似肥皂剧的情节。

segments.textEn: Please feel free to share all of that, whatever you're comfortable sharing. We'd love to hear whatever you can legally share.
segments.textZh: 请随意分享所有这些，任何你愿意分享的内容。无论有什么是你在法律上可以分享的，我们都很想听听。

segments.textEn: Yeah, absolutely. Well, I'll try to actually. I'll focus on the non personnel.
segments.textZh: 是的，当然。好吧，我会试着，实际上。我会把重点放在非人事方面。

segments.textEn: Fair enough.
segments.textZh: 很合理。

segments.textEn: Because I think that's more pertinent for the future in terms of where do we come from, where are we headed? And that kind of thing. So in starting a car company, it's obviously a high capital endeavor and particularly when you're talking about something which is a brand new technology and no one had really gotten all the pieces to work together quite right.
segments.textZh: 因为我认为，就我们的来路、我们的去向以及诸如此类的问题而言，那与未来更为相关。所以，创办一家汽车公司显然是一项资本密集型事业，尤其是当你谈论的是一种全新的技术，而且还没有人真正把所有部分相当妥善地整合起来的时候。

segments.textEn: To create a compelling product. As far as electric cars are concerned,
segments.textZh: 以创造出一款有吸引力的产品。就电动汽车而言，

segments.textEn: there's a couple of people who tried and companies that came and went well,
segments.textZh: 有几个人尝试过，也有一些公司来了又走了，嗯，

segments.textEn: and some of those companies are sort of still here today. Like General motors had the EV1, and actually if they'd continued and produced the EV2, EV3 and continued that development, there probably wouldn't have been a need for Tesla. But they didn't, unfortunately. They took those cars away from people forcibly and crushed them.
segments.textZh: 而其中一些公司某种程度上至今仍然存在。比如通用汽车曾有 EV1，事实上，如果他们继续下去，生产 EV2、EV3，并继续这项研发，或许就没有创办 Tesla 的必要了。但遗憾的是，他们没有这么做。他们强行从人们手中收走了那些汽车，并把它们压碎了。

segments.textEn: Literally crushed them. And if people have seen Chris Payne's movie who Killed the Electric Car? Which I recommend, you can see some of that.
segments.textZh: 真的是把它们压碎了。如果大家看过克里斯·佩恩的电影《谁消灭了电动车？》——我推荐这部电影——就能看到其中一些情况。

segments.textEn: It's amazing that the people who Jim gave those EV ones to held a candlelit vigil for their cars getting crushed. I mean, can you imagine anyone holding a can look visual for a GM car?
segments.textZh: 令人惊讶的是，那些获赠吉姆送出的 EV 1 的人，竟然为自己的汽车被压碎举行了烛光守夜活动。我的意思是，你能想象有人为一辆通用汽车举行一场“罐头样的视觉活动”吗？

segments.textEn: No, I really can't.
segments.textZh: 不，我确实无法想象。

segments.textEn: Or any product.
segments.textZh: 或者任何产品。

segments.textEn: Or any product is the point.
segments.textZh: 重点是，或者任何产品。

segments.textEn: Why would you discontinue a product line with that level of customer interest? That's pretty amazing.
segments.textZh: 为什么要停产一个拥有如此高客户兴趣的产品线？这相当令人惊讶。

segments.textEn: Yeah, it's pretty well documented in that film. Okay, so but I'll give you the
segments.textZh: 是的，那部电影对此有相当充分的记录。好，那么，不过我会给你……

segments.textEn: chronology and the reasoning. Why did we start with the car that we started with? Because I do get asked the question, why are you making this expensive sports car?
segments.textZh: 时间顺序和背后的理由。为什么我们从最初选择的那款车开始？因为我确实经常被问到这个问题：为什么你们要制造这种昂贵的跑车？

segments.textEn: Implying that we somehow think there's a shortage of sports cars in the world. Or rich people really need a break or something like that. It's absurd if you think of it, but nonetheless, people get a little confused, like why can't you make it an affordable car?
segments.textZh: 这暗示我们不知为何认为世界上缺少跑车。或者富人确实需要得到一点优待之类的。你仔细想想，这很荒谬，但尽管如此，人们还是会有点困惑，比如你们为什么不能造一辆价格亲民的汽车？

segments.textEn: I wanted to give you the opportunity to explain.
segments.textZh: 我想给你这个解释的机会。

segments.textEn: Yeah, absolutely.
segments.textZh: 是的，当然。

segments.textEn: And there are two reasons. One. One is that when you have a brand new technology, it tends to be expensive. It's almost always expensive, in fact, because the first thing you're trying to do is to make it work. And if you're just trying to make it work, you don't have an opportunity to optimize the cost. And if you think about anything new, when cell phones first came out, they were very expensive.
segments.textZh: 这有2个原因。第1个。第1个是，当你拥有一种全新的技术时，它往往很昂贵。事实上，它几乎总是很昂贵，因为你首先要做的是让它能够运作。而如果你只是试图让它运作起来，就没有机会优化成本。如果你想想任何新事物，手机刚问世时，它们非常昂贵。

segments.textEn: Personal computers were very expensive. Even gasoline engine cars in the beginning were very, very expensive. Could only be afforded by a few people.
segments.textZh: 个人电脑曾经非常昂贵。甚至汽油发动机汽车在一开始也非常、非常昂贵。只有少数人负担得起。

segments.textEn: Absolutely.
segments.textZh: 当然。

segments.textEn: Who doesn't remember the $1,400 VCR? Right.
segments.textZh: 谁不记得那台1,400美元的录像机？对吧。

segments.textEn: Absolutely.
segments.textZh: 当然。

segments.textEn: It's part of our.
segments.textZh: 这是我们……的一部分。

segments.textEn: In fact, you can point at almost anything new innovation. It starts off expensive because the first thing you're trying to do is make it work.
segments.textZh: 事实上，你几乎可以指向任何新的创新。它刚开始时都很昂贵，因为你首先要做的是让它能够运作。

segments.textEn: Cell phones the size of a shoebox, $1,800.
segments.textZh: 鞋盒那么大的手机，1,800美元。

segments.textEn: I remember Wall street with the guy walking around with that shoebox phone, basically. So a new technology is expensive. And then the other factor is economies of scale. So in order to make something inexpensive, you have to make a lot of it. But to put together a factory that can make hundreds of thousands of cars costs a billion dollars or more.
segments.textZh: 我记得《华尔街》里有个人拿着那种鞋盒般的手机走来走去，基本上就是如此。所以新技术很昂贵。然后另一个因素是规模经济。因此，要想让某样东西变得便宜，你就必须大量生产。但要建成一座能够生产数十万辆汽车的工厂，需要花费10亿美元或更多。

segments.textEn: And who's going to take a chance?
segments.textZh: 谁会愿意冒这个险？

segments.textEn: Right. And the thing is, it would still be silly to try to do that economies of scale thing on the first iteration of technology because it's still going to be expensive. And this is a problem that GM is starting to see with the bolt because they're having trouble bringing the cost of that car below $40,000. And that's problematic when you're talking about a car that is essentially intended to compete against gasoline cars that are in the 25 to $30,000 range.
segments.textZh: 对。问题是，在技术的第一次迭代中尝试实现规模经济仍然是愚蠢的，因为它的成本仍然会很高。这也是通用汽车开始在 Bolt 上看到的问题，因为他们很难把那款车的成本降到40,000美元以下。而当你谈论的是一款本质上旨在与价格处于25到30,000美元区间的汽油车竞争的汽车时，这就成了问题。

segments.textEn: It's very important that an electric car be of comparable price to other cars of its type. So the Tesla Roadster is actually about the same price as a Porsche.
segments.textZh: 电动汽车的价格与同类型的其他汽车相当，这一点非常重要。所以 Tesla Roadster 的价格实际上和保时捷差不多。

segments.textEn: In many cases less.
segments.textZh: 很多情况下价格还要更低。

segments.textEn: Yeah. In fact, less than a Porsche Turbo. So anyway, so that's basically the reason it was the first generation of technology and we were necessarily at low volume because we didn't have the capital to go to high volume manufacturing.
segments.textZh: 对。事实上，比保时捷 Turbo 还便宜。所以不管怎样，基本原因就是，这是第一代技术，而且我们必然只能进行小批量生产，因为我们没有资本转向大批量制造。

segments.textEn: Yeah. And you weren't making an inexpensive sports car. You were making a brand new, state of the art sports car. That was some of the negativity that I didn't Understand, because it didn't seem to come from naive people. It seemed to come from people who seemed very scholar in their particular areas of expertise, who completely missed the obvious justification in terms of what kind of vehicle you were actually making from the ground up.
segments.textZh: 对。而且你们造的并不是一款廉价跑车。你们造的是一款全新的、最先进的跑车。那些负面评价中，有一些是我无法理解的，因为它们似乎并不是来自无知的人。它们似乎来自那些在各自专业领域中显得很有学问的人，但他们完全忽略了一个显而易见的合理理由，也就是你们实际上是在从零开始制造什么类型的车辆。

segments.textEn: And it being the first of its kind, I'm astounded by.
segments.textZh: 而且它还是同类中的第一款，我对……感到非常惊叹。

segments.textEn: Well, a common misperception is that because for the roadster, we worked with Lotus and we did initially intend to use a modified Lotus Elise chassis for our car, people think, oh, it's just a modified Lotus.
